aliases.description: Other handles of the same bytes (an `md5` item's `b3` twin).

size.description: Bytes, checked against what is read (spec 18).

Caps.description: Capability strings (spec 5.3); unknown strings are ignored

base.description: The base it is built on (`plumcraft 0.1.0`).

Column.description: A table column: its name and the wire type of its values.

Compat.description: An extra conversion a port accepts.

DataRef.description:
A handle plus typed metadata plus the ways to reach the bytes, in the engine's order of
preference.

at.description: Unknown or malformed locators are skipped.

handle.description:
`None` only for a protocol 1 array published without a commonkit key; the reader may
hash the file if it needs an identity (spec 17).

Display.description: What the viewer shows for one watched value.

full.description: The value itself, read lazily (probe, compare, playback, 1:1 zoom).

items.description: Items in the list (1 for a single value) and the one shown.

recipe.description: What made the item shown: `{style?, params, settings, graph}`.

Editor.description: A custom editor: `curves`, `mask` or a pack kind, on a port.

EngineInfo.description: Who answered, and what its results depend on.

salt.description: The engine's code digest, part of every memo key (spec 14).

schema_digest.description: Lets the UI skip a catalogue it has cached.

EngineState.description:
What the host reports about its engine (spec 12.4). Engines push only states only they know
(`unavailable`); every other state is the host's.

oneOf.description: A broker or server that can't be reached, with the fix.
The engine isn't running or crashed, with the fix (from the engine manifest).
Up but unusable (no GPU device, protocol mismatch).
Missed pings during a run.

ErrorData.description: `{kind, hint?}` attached to a protocol error.

Export.description:
Whether a node can be marked for export (a Cartooner checkpoint), and what core calls the
mark. The pack's export data is opaque.

Family.description: A node family: nodes are coloured by family (theme tokens, by id).

Form.description:
What the bytes hold, enough to choose a viewer before reading them. An unknown kind reads as
[`Form::Bytes`].

oneOf.description: PCM stored as (frames, channels).
SVG and similar.
An encoded source picture.
An application document (an artcraft file).
Named typed columns (media `table`), stored as JSON `{"columns": [{name, type, values}]}`.

GraphRef.description: The graph a run executes: the workflow JSON inline, or a handle from `graph.put`.

Hello.description: UI → engine: open (or resume) a session.

session.description: The session to resume, and the last envelope `seq` the client applied.

token.description: Required on sockets and non-loopback HTTP. Never logged ([`Hello::redacted`]).

HostInfo.description: The client's host, for the same-host proof and store roots.

Limits.description: Session limits (spec 5.2). Absent fields take these defaults.

LiveMark.description: Whether a display is a provisional value from a node still running (spec 10.6).

LiveUpdate.description: Live data in flight for a watched value (spec 10.6).

oneOf.description: A whole provisional value; the newest per (node, port) wins.

A growing value with a contiguous `offset`; a gap makes the viewer fetch `run.get`
partials.

ref.description: A chunk too large to inline.

oneOf.description: A node-scoped message: status tooltip and run log, never the value.

Locator.description:
One way to reach a blob's bytes. Readers take the first they can use, cheapest first:
`mem`, `commonkit`, `path`, their own CAS by handle, `url`, then a derivative request.
`commonkit` and `path` are honoured only after the same-host proof, under declared roots
(spec 4.4, 5.4).

oneOf.description: A commonkit key, resolved under the reader's own store root.
A file on the same host; `offset` into the payload of a wrapping `.npy`.
In-process binding only: a slot in the host's byte table.
Base64 bytes, at most the session's inline limit.

op_id.description: The request this log belongs to (a long `x.vi.deliver`).

Media.description: Media kinds (spec 10.1): how a value is shown. A closed set; unknown reads as `bytes`.

oneOf.description: Opaque: the hex viewer plus any rgba8 rendition. Also what an unknown kind reads as.

MemoInfo.description: A node's memo identity in this run (spec 14).

computed_ms.description: What computing this result took, when it was computed or a record says.

source.description:
Where a cached result came from: `memory`, `store` or `content` (found by its inputs'
bytes, not how they were made). Absent when the node ran.

MemoMode.description: How a run uses the memo. The exactness and conformance gates send `off` with a fresh store.

oneOf.description: Recompute the targets, keep upstream results.
The default; also what an unknown mode reads as.

MemoScope.description: Where a node's results may be reused (spec 14.4).

oneOf.description: The default; also what an unknown scope reads as.

content.description: Ask for a content key as well as a plan key.

NodeDef.description: One node type. Rust never hard-codes one.

engines.description:
In a catalogue merged from several (a coordinator's, spec 7.3): the engines that offer
this kind, the one that runs it unless the workflow says otherwise first. Absent from a
single engine's catalogue.

version.description: Part of the memo key; absent → 1.

NodeError.description:
A node's or a run's error, as data. `kind` is one of [`NodeError::KINDS`]; an unknown kind is
kept as text and shown as an operation error.

type.description: The exception type, when there was one.

bundle_port.description: The input that takes the parameter bundle (protocol 1: `settings`).

keep.description: `true`, `false` or `"unit"`: whether results keep colour-space tags.

recipe.description: The input whose recipes this node gets as its `recipe` value.

result.description: A result node: its output is the graph's result (protocol 1: `vi.op.result`).

vary_choices.description: Its `values` text is seeded with the choices of the ENUM input it is wired into.

editor.description: Editor payloads by editor kind (`curves`, `mask`); opaque to core.

provenance.description: Where each input's value came from: wire | bundle | widget | default.

text.description: Text the node shows (a summary, a warning about an unused override).

NodeSnapshot.description: A node as `run.get` sees it now.

NodeState.description:
A node's state (spec 9.4). Every UI accepts all nine; an unknown state is
[`NodeState::Unknown`] and its record is ignored.

oneOf.description: Adds thumb, outputs and displays; never changes a terminal state.

ParamRef.description: The bundle parameter a port is tied to (protocol 1's impressionist `setting{section, name}`).

Partial.description: An appending value's bytes so far.

PathHint.description: What a path input names, for its file dialog: `open`, `save` or `folder`.

PeekReply.description: `{display}` now, `{pending}` (it arrives on a `preview` record), or `{missing}`.

PeekRequest.description: `run.peek`: open any (node, port, index) of a run without a new run.

PlanReply.description: `run.plan`: order, plan keys and cached states without running.

Port.description: One input or output of a node. Every protocol 1 field keeps its meaning.

active_when.description: Read only under these parameters' values.

disabled_choices.description: Choices that can't run on this machine → why.

external.description: A group shows this port on its surface, wired or not.

fills.description: A choice that fills other ports: `{choice: {port: value}}`. The filled ports stay editable.

shows.description: With `fills`: the ports each choice uses, which the node shows.

socket.description: `None`: the type's default ([`Socket::Both`] for scalars, [`Socket::Socket`] otherwise).

soft_min.description: The span a slider covers when narrower than `min..max`, or when a bound is open.

widget.description: How to show the value when its type alone doesn't say. Unknown hints are ignored.

PortValue.description: A port value in a reply, snapshot or event (spec 4.5).

oneOf.description: Numbers, bools, strings, settings, curves.
A value the engine keeps to itself (a STYLE), with a line describing it.

held.description:
The engine still has it (`values.held`, spec 7.6 rule 11): pass it back to that
engine as an input of the same run.

PreviewSizes.description: Thumbnail and viewer sizes (long side, pixels).

Proof.description: One direction of the same-host proof (spec 5.4): a nonce file the other side reads.

client_proof_read.description: In the engine's reply: it read the client's nonce file and it matched.

ProtoError.description: A request that failed as a request: `{code, message, data?}`.

ProtocolRange.description: A range of protocol majors one side speaks.

Rendition.description: An engine-made derivative the UI draws without understanding the value (spec 10.3).

items.description: List length when the value is a list (0: a single value).

summary.description: A one-line description of the value ("array HSI 64×80 float32").

oneOf.description: (levels, channels, bins, 2) min/max.
(frames, bins) f32 dB.
Up to 4 KiB of text and where it sits.
Small inline series.
Inline JSON, depth ≤ 32.

Replay.description: Whether a resumed session's missed events were replayed.

oneOf.description: The ring no longer covers `since`: the engine emits `resync`; the client calls `run.get`.

Resync.description: The client must call `run.get`: events were lost or the ring no longer covers it.

RunAck.description: The immediate answer to `run`; the result arrives as a `run.reply` event.

RunReply.description: `run.reply`: authoritative. The reducer fills every node without a record from it.

engine_stats.description: A coordinator's run: each engine's share.

stats.description: What the run's caches did (spec 14.6): the whole run's, across its engines.

watch.description: In request order; an entry with only `error` set says why there is no display.

detach.description: Survive the session going idle, for `run_ttl_s`.

generation.description: Monotonic per session; records and replies of older generations are ignored.

hold.description: `node.port`s whose value the engine keeps for this run if it can't send it (spec 7.6 rule 11).

inputs.description:
`{"node.port": value}`: external bindings that override a port's wire or widget.
Joins graphs across engines (decision D14) and lets a client feed a node a value; spec 7.6 rule 10.

scope.description:
The life of the graph this run belongs to, from its opening to the next: what the engine
keeps for it (scratch files) goes on `graph.release`. Empty: unscoped (spec 5.3).

targets.description: Empty: the graph's sinks. Watched nodes are added by the engine.

trusted_roots.description: Folders besides its store where this run's `path` locators may be read (spec 7.6 rule 10).

RunSnapshot.description: `run.get`: the resync path, mandatory on every engine (spec 8.5).

last_seq.description: The last envelope `seq` this snapshot includes.

watch.description: One per watch entry; `None` until it exists.

RunStats.description: What a run's caches did (capability `run.stats`, spec 14.6).

computed_ms.description: What the nodes that ran took, and what the hits would have taken.

from_memory.description: Nodes answered by the in-memory memo, by a persisted record, and by a content key.

kept.description: Records written, so a later run or process can skip the node.

store.description: The store's own counters over the run, by contract name (`shm_hit`, `shm_declined_space`).

store_missed.description: Persistable nodes with no usable record.

tree.description: The tree, when its usage is known.

media.description: The kinds of value it writes. Empty: any.

inputs.description: What crosses into this engine's share of a larger graph, as `RunRequest.inputs`.

path.description: Omitted when `data.path` is off: the files come back as blobs.

recipe_graph.description: The whole graph that share came from: what a saved recipe holds, so it remakes the file.

expansions.description: Command node id → the graph it unrolls into. Opaque.

templates.description: Name → a graph the UI opens (protocol 1 `style_graphs`).

SessionConfirm.description: UI → engine after `hello`: the same-host verdicts (spec 5.4).

path.description: The engine read the UI's nonce: the engine may read paths the UI names.

shm.description: The UI read the engine's nonce: engine `commonkit`/`path` locators are usable.

SheetCell.description: One item of a list as the sheet shows it.

label.description: What made it differ from the others ("dim 150 · resample bilinear").

Socket.description: How a port appears on a node.

oneOf.description: A plain widget; cannot be wired.
Wire only; no widget.
A widget that becomes a socket when wired.

blob.description: Stats too large to carry inline, as a JSON blob (spec 10.2).

display.description: `preview` of a watched node with `display.stream` on: one per watch entry for it.

publisher.description: A stable id of the emitting process instance.

seq.description:
The record's own counter, per publisher and run (protocol 1's `seq`). With `publisher`,
it orders a node's records and drops redeliveries.

TreeUsage.description:
The store tree as a run left it. Its size comes from the reaper's last walk and can be
unknown; the disk's free space is always read, and is what the store refuses writes by.

free_bytes.description: Free space on the store's disk, and the floor under which the store refuses writes.

View.description: A view of a value: an id the wire type lists, and its parameters.

Want.description:
A derivative the viewer wants: `{"kind": "rgba8"}`, `{"kind": "peaks", "px": 1600}`,
`{"kind": "full"}`. Parameters are kind-specific and kept as JSON.

WatchRequest.description: One value the UI wants to see while (or after) a run (spec 10.4; protocol 1 `inspect`).

px.description: The long side of view renditions.

sheet.description: Every item of a list, small and labelled.

WireType.description: A wire type: its colour and how its values are shown.

thumb.description: Whether node thumbnails are drawn for it.

views.description: The views the viewer offers, exactly (replaces a hard-coded list).

description: The UI <-> engine interface (docs/interface.md). An envelope's body is one of: EngineState (engine.state), StatusRecord (node.status), LiveUpdate (node.live), RunReply (run.reply), LogRecord (log), Resync (resync), {schema_digest} (schema.changed).
title: PlumCraft protocol 2
